Reason with explicit program structures, anchoring every claim to narrow snippet ranges and requiring both source (attacker-controlled input/payload/index) and sink (memory access, dereference, write, authorization decision, format/string operation) quoted together with line ranges before any vulnerability conclusion. Sequence — ordered data-flow from attacker-controlled sources through transformations to sinks. Step 1: identify attacker-controlled sources. Quote each source snippet (≤3 lines, exact start/end with line numbers), including derived pointers/indexes from untrusted counts; for derived-pointer sources quote both parent-assigned derived pointer expression and its origin from untrusted parsing together, anchored to exact parsing line; explicitly distinguish raw attacker input from parsed/derived values and quote the parsing expression separately. Step 2: trace derived pointer/index assignment through each transformation; at each step quote assignment and the consuming operation together with both line ranges, state "assignment unvalidated" if no guard quotes validity before use; prioritize derived-pointer validity at sink by quoting exact sink dereference/assignment/write line and stating "derived-pointer validity at sink never quoted" when unquoted — treat absence as confidence limitation, never vulnerability evidence; when index derived from array length or untrusted count, quote both derivation expression and the consuming access with separate ranges; if loop writes to derived pointer, quote derived assignment + loop-access + loop bound as three separate snippet pairs, never merging into one block. Before any vulnerability claim, confirm sink line quoted separately with its own range and both source/sink paired; if snippet exceeds 3 lines state "inference: snippet spans >3 lines; confidence reduced"; when sink line cannot be inferred directly, reduce confidence to ≤0.35 and do not assign CWE. Step 3: verify validation at every transition; identify missing intermediate validation specifically for derived pointer/index at sink; confirm unguarded path by quoting guard-absent sink line; do not claim vulnerability without both source and sink quoted separately in ≤3-line pairs; for loop-derived access quote index derivation + loop-access separately with both ranges; specifically check index/offset derivation from untrusted input at loop entry, verify bounds check occurs BEFORE access with quoted snippet pair covering both lines, and state "loop-bound from untrusted count" when applicable; verify termination exits dangerous path with quoted termination line; for derived-pointer loops, insist on separate evidence for derived assignment, index derivation, loop bound, loop write, and guard on derived object — if any missing, treat as unguarded only when sink quoted, else do not claim vulnerability. Branch — for each if/else, state condition controlling attacker input. Confirm guard is BEFORE dangerous operation (G before S with quoted G and S). Verify missing break/return/continue allows fallthrough past guard to sink; quote guard and fallthrough path with both line numbers. Check operator correctness (> vs >=, off-by-one, unsigned wrap, underflow/overflow, sign-mismatch) with quoted snippet including line numbers; quote the guard's comparison expression with its line number and the sink's access line separately. Confirm guard applies to sink's accessed object: explicitly state "mismatch: guard checks parent (X) at G but sink dereferences derived pointer (Y) at S" with both line numbers as separate snippet pairs; when derived pointer unvalidated at sink treat path as unguarded rather than relying on parent check; for authorization confirm success/failure assignment cannot be unconditionally overwritten, quote both with ranges; quote each branch sink independently and do not claim branch-controlled vulnerability if sink line is missing; for multi-branch code, quote sink for every branch that reaches a dangerous operation and confirm guard applies to that branch's specific object. Loop — for each for/while state bound (constant/parsed/user/array-length from untrusted). Quote index derivation expression + array/structure access together (≤3 lines including index expression and access/write). Confirm index/offset/count derived from untrusted input; verify bounds check occurs BEFORE access with quoted snippet pair (check line + access line). When loop writes through derived pointer quote derived assignment + loop access together with both ranges; confirm guard applies to derived pointer, not only parent — state "guard applies to parent (P) at G but loop accesses derived pointer (D) at L" if mismatch. Verify termination exits dangerous path; quote termination snippet with line number; verify loop bounds against structure sizes with quoted pairs covering bound expression and access; before loop-based claim confirm both index-derivation and loop-access snippets separately quoted with ranges; if either >3 lines reduce confidence; specifically for index derived from offset/count, quote derivation expression at its assignment line and loop access at its use line as independent pairs. Sink-order analysis (addressing localization/ordering failure): before assigning CWE or confidence, identify the exact dangerous operation type in order of observability — (a) direct memory dereference/write via pointer/index at specific line, (b) authorization/auth decision overwrite/branch bypass, (c) arithmetic/integer operation at sink, (d) format/string operation at sink. Quote the sink snippet containing the exact write/dereference/assignment/format line; if sink line must be inferred rather than directly quoted, reduce confidence to ≤0.35 and do not assign CWE; do not claim memory vulnerability from format-string absence alone. For derived-pointer loops: quote derived assignment, index derivation, loop bound, loop write, and any guard on derived pointer separately; do not merge into a single multi-line snippet. Evidence anchoring (addressing sparse/low-specificity evidence): for every vulnerability claim include at least three evidence items — one for source/derived-pointer assignment (with range), one for sink (with exact range containing dangerous operation), and one for validation/guard state at transition (with both guard and sink line when relevant); all must be ≤3 lines and independently quoted; include derived-pointer assignment + sink pair with both ranges when derived pointer involved; include guard-object mismatch statement as separate evidence when applicable; state whether guard applies to attacker-controlled path; include exact dereference/assignment/write lines; prefer narrow ranges (≤3) for high confidence, wider only unavoidable with stated reduction; when derived-pointer validity at sink unquoted, include explicit limitation note rather than using absence as evidence. CWE identification (select only from observable sink type, addressing misidentification from inference): memory dereference/access = CWE-787/125/416; input validation failure at sink = CWE-20; authorization/auth bypass = CWE-287/862; arithmetic/integer at sink = CWE-190/191; format/string = CWE-134/78; select most specific directly observable from quoted sink snippet, not from validation behavior or absence alone; prefer observable sink over inference; list at most one CWE unless multiple clearly distinct sink types in different branches visible; do NOT list CWE when only source is quoted and sink is missing/inferred, when only guard absence is noted without quoted sink, when sink is format/string but format string is literal (attacker controls only data argument), or when only validation behavior is described; if no dangerous sink quoted, omit CWE entirely; when sink is memory write through derived pointer, prefer CWE-787; never assign CWE based solely on unquoted derived-pointer validity or guard absence. Reason with explicit program structures, anchoring every claim to narrow snippet ranges and requiring both source (attacker-controlled input/payload/index) and sink (memory access, dereference, write, authorization decision, format/string operation) quoted together with line ranges before any vulnerability conclusion. Sequence — ordered data-flow from attacker-controlled sources through transformations to sinks. Step 1: identify attacker-controlled sources. Quote each source snippet (≤3 lines, exact start/end with line numbers), including derived pointers/indexes from untrusted counts; for derived-pointer sources quote both parent-assigned derived pointer expression and its origin from untrusted parsing together, anchored to exact parsing line; explicitly distinguish raw attacker input from parsed/derived values and quote the parsing expression separately. Step 2: trace derived pointer/index assignment through each transformation; at each step quote assignment and the consuming operation together with both line ranges, state "assignment unvalidated" if no guard quotes validity before use; prioritize derived-pointer validity at sink by quoting exact sink dereference/assignment/write line and stating "derived-pointer validity at sink never quoted" when unquoted — treat absence as confidence limitation, never vulnerability evidence; when index derived from array length or untrusted count, quote both derivation expression and the consuming access with separate ranges; if loop writes to derived pointer, quote derived assignment + loop-access + loop bound as three separate snippet pairs, never merging into one block. Before any vulnerability claim, confirm sink line quoted separately with its own range and both source/sink paired; if snippet exceeds 3 lines state "inference: snippet spans >3 lines; confidence reduced"; when sink line cannot be inferred directly, reduce confidence to ≤0.35 and do not assign CWE. Step 3: verify validation at every transition; identify missing intermediate validation specifically for derived pointer/index at sink; confirm unguarded path by quoting guard-absent sink line; do not claim vulnerability without both source and sink quoted separately in ≤3-line pairs; for loop-derived access quote index derivation + loop-access separately with both ranges; specifically check index/offset derivation from untrusted input at loop entry, verify bounds check occurs BEFORE access with quoted snippet pair covering both lines, and state "loop-bound from untrusted count" when applicable; verify termination exits dangerous path with quoted termination line; for derived-pointer loops, insist on separate evidence for derived assignment, index derivation, loop bound, loop write, and guard on derived object — if any missing, treat as unguarded only when sink quoted, else do not claim vulnerability. Branch — for each if/else, state condition controlling attacker input. Confirm guard is BEFORE dangerous operation (G before S with quoted G and S). Verify missing break/return/continue allows fallthrough past guard to sink; quote guard and fallthrough path with both line numbers. Check operator correctness (> vs >=, off-by-one, unsigned wrap, underflow/overflow, sign-mismatch) with quoted snippet including line numbers; quote the guard's comparison expression with its line number and the sink's access line separately. Confirm guard applies to sink's accessed object: explicitly state "mismatch: guard checks parent (X) at G but sink dereferences derived pointer (Y) at S" with both line numbers as separate snippet pairs; when derived pointer unvalidated at sink treat path as unguarded rather than relying on parent check; for authorization confirm success/failure assignment cannot be unconditionally overwritten, quote both with ranges; quote each branch sink independently and do not claim branch-controlled vulnerability if sink line is missing; for multi-branch code, quote sink for every branch that reaches a dangerous operation and confirm guard applies to that branch's specific object. Loop — for each for/while state bound (constant/parsed/user/array-length from untrusted). Quote index derivation expression + array/structure access together (≤3 lines including index expression and access/write). Confirm index/offset/count derived from untrusted input; verify bounds check occurs BEFORE access with quoted snippet pair (check line + access line). When loop writes through derived pointer quote derived assignment + loop access together with both ranges; confirm guard applies to derived pointer, not only parent — state "guard applies to parent (P) at G but loop accesses derived pointer (D) at L" if mismatch. Verify termination exits dangerous path; quote termination snippet with line number; verify loop bounds against structure sizes with quoted pairs covering bound expression and access; before loop-based claim confirm both index-derivation and loop-access snippets separately quoted with ranges; if either >3 lines reduce confidence; specifically for index derived from offset/count, quote derivation expression at its assignment line and loop access at its use line as independent pairs. Sink-order analysis (addressing localization/ordering failure): before assigning CWE or confidence, identify the exact dangerous operation type in order of observability — (a) direct memory dereference/write via pointer/index at specific line, (b) authorization/auth decision overwrite/branch bypass, (c) arithmetic/integer operation at sink, (d) format/string operation at sink. Quote the sink snippet containing the exact write/dereference/assignment/format line; if sink line must be inferred rather than directly quoted, reduce confidence to ≤0.35 and do not assign CWE; do not claim memory vulnerability from format-string absence alone. For derived-pointer loops: quote derived assignment, index derivation, loop bound, loop write, and any guard on derived pointer separately; do not merge into a single multi-line snippet. Evidence anchoring (addressing sparse/low-specificity evidence): for every vulnerability claim include at least three evidence items — one for source/derived-pointer assignment (with range), one for sink (with exact range containing dangerous operation), and one for validation/guard state at transition (with both guard and sink line when relevant); all must be ≤3 lines and independently quoted; include derived-pointer assignment + sink pair with both ranges when derived pointer involved; include guard-object mismatch statement as separate evidence when applicable; state whether guard applies to attacker-controlled path; include exact dereference/assignment/write lines; prefer narrow ranges (≤3) for high confidence, wider only unavoidable with stated reduction; when derived-pointer validity at sink unquoted, include explicit limitation note rather than using absence as evidence. CWE identification (select only from observable sink type, addressing misidentification from inference): memory dereference/access = CWE-787/125/416; input validation failure at sink = CWE-20; authorization/auth bypass = CWE-287/862; arithmetic/integer at sink = CWE-190/191; format/string = CWE-134/78; select most specific directly observable from quoted sink snippet, not from validation behavior or absence alone; prefer observable sink over inference; list at most one CWE unless multiple clearly distinct sink types in different branches visible; do NOT list CWE when only source is quoted and sink is missing/inferred, when only guard absence is noted without quoted sink, when sink is format/string but format string is literal (attacker controls only data argument), or when only validation behavior is described; if no dangerous sink quoted, omit CWE entirely; when sink is memory write through derived pointer, prefer CWE-787; never assign CWE based solely on unquoted derived-pointer validity or guard absence.
